text: H1 (behaviour exists): On custom prompts of the form '... a pear. ... the {X} tree/seller/box ... picked/sold me/there was', GPT-2 small prefers ' an' over ' a' when X is a vowel-initial noun (apple, orange, egg, onion...) and ' a' when X is consonant-initial (lemon, peach...). Clean = vowel noun, corrupt = consonant noun in the same slot, same token count. Metric: logit(' an') - logit(' a'). Counts against: clean logit diff <= 0 or not clearly above corrupt logit diff; or token-length mismatch in pairs (then fix the pairs).
Tests H1: does the model do a/an at all on my hand-written pairs, and are pairs token-aligned?

E0001 (local-full, full precision): on 18 hand-written pairs incl. the user's own example sentence, GPT-2 small does NOT output ' an'. Clean (vowel noun) logit diff an-a = -3.01 +/- 0.53, accuracy 0/18 (top prediction ' a' in every case). Corrupt (consonant noun) = -3.54. So there is only a weak shift of ~+0.53 logits toward ' an', never enough to flip the choice. The user's example 'I climbed up the pear tree ... apple tree and picked' gives -3.54 (predicts ' a'). H1 as stated is contradicted for these templates.

H2 (behaviour exists under stronger context): the failure in E0001 is template-specific; with prompts that constrain the next noun more strongly (comma-list parallel structure; 'X: I want' pattern; few-shot 'word: article word' lists that contain both a and an examples in clean AND corrupt so the article cannot be copied differentially) the clean logit diff becomes positive. Counts against: clean logit diff stays negative in all styles -> the model does not do the behaviour, stop and report. Mixed-style baseline: prompts 0-3 comma-list, 4-7 'X: I want', 8-13 few-shot with both articles, 14-17 'This is the X. It is'.
Tests H2: does any stronger prompt style produce a positive an-a logit diff? Index: 0-3 comma list, 4-7 'Want X: I want', 8-13 few-shot both articles, 14-17 short declaratives.

E0002 (local-full, full precision): 18 new pairs in 4 stronger styles. Clean an-a logit diff is negative in all 18 (mean -2.37 +/- 1.13, accuracy 0/18); corrupt mean -3.33. By style (clean / corrupt means): comma-list -2.42 / -3.59; 'Want X: I want' -4.17 / -5.44; few-shot with both articles in context -1.33 / -2.40 (best single prompt -0.71); short declaratives -2.06 / -2.36. Across E0001+E0002 the vowel noun raises the diff in 36/36 pairs (mean shift +0.53 and +0.96) but never makes ' an' beat ' a'.
Rejected by E0001: clean logit diff -3.01, accuracy 0/18, including the user's example sentence. Only a sub-threshold shift of +0.53 vs corrupt.
Rejected by E0002: clean logit diff negative in 18/18 prompts across four stronger styles (best -0.71), accuracy 0/18. The failure is not template-specific.

Stop per step 1 of the protocol: gpt2 (small) on local-full does not perform the stated behaviour (0/36 clean prompts choose ' an' in E0001+E0002). No mechanism experiments run, no verify_hypothesis run, because there is no behaviour to explain. What exists is a consistent but sub-threshold sensitivity (vowel noun raises an-a by ~0.5-1.0 logits in 36/36 pairs); its mechanism is unmeasured. Options for the user: (a) investigate that weak shift in gpt2 as a 'partial sensitivity' study, (b) rerun on a larger model that actually flips to ' an'. 38 of 40 experiments unused.
